review: 1:1 שֵׁם יֵשׁוּעַ מָתֹק מְאֹד — the Arabic is a verb ('the name has grown sweet'); Hebrew uses a verbless clause because a finite verb here would push the line past 8.
3:4 לְאָזְנַי יֶעֱרָב — עָרַב, 'be sweet/pleasant' (Jer 31:26, Prov 13:19); the Arabic repeats the sweetness image of 1:1, and Hebrew keeps the repetition.

4:3–4:4 יֵבוֹשׁ ... כִּי־מָצָאתִי חֵן שָׁלֵם — the Arabic has 'when I find from Him full acceptance'; the Hebrew recasts it as the enemy seeing that I have found full favour, which is the sense of the clause.
5:1 רַךְ לְבָבִי עוֹזְרִי — 'my heart is weak, my Helper'; the Arabic يَا مُعِين is vocative, Hebrew drops the particle to keep the line short.
6:4 כַּאֲשֶׁר נָאוָה — 'as is fitting'; the phrase echoes Ps 33:1 לַיְשָׁרִים נָאוָה תְהִלָּה, for سُبْحًا كَمَا وَجَب.
